title: Hines, Dave Payton, Francois's band and quitting whiskey
summary: Punch talks about covering for Earl Hines's band, the Regal Theater opening with Payton, five years with Francois and its breakup, and quitting drinking in 1941.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Did you ever work with Errol Hines?

Well, no, not, I have worked in his spot, you know what I mean, like this. See, they went off, and we taking their place for a few days. We was a little Louisiana band I had. Mm-hmm. We had, and until they come back, then they went back on the job. But I never worked in his band. Mm-hmm. Tell no lie about it.
What about Dave Payton? Did you ever work with him?
Yeah, I worked with him at the Regal Theater when it first opened up. Mm-hmm.
And who, which other bands were you working with while you were working with Dave Payton?

Well, to tell the truth, I was still with the Lusianans. Mm-hmm. But Dave Payton was just getting up a, what do you call it, something like an all-star band to make a big opening there, see. Mm-hmm. And he made that big opening for two days, Saturday and Sunday I think it was. All day Sunday and Saturday night. And then after that he had got his regular band, you know, what he wanted there, but I was still with Francois Lusianan. Mm-hmm. Yeah. I see. So, how many years were you with Francois? Well I'm going to be straight with you. I'm telling you, I stayed with him longer than I did any band in Chicago, I know that. Mm-hmm. He was a little band, we were just all boys from New Orleans, you know, we just stuck together, just like that. Mm-hmm. And how we broke up was when the place caught a fire and Francois was the type of fellow that didn't finally get around and look for nothing, see. Mm-hmm. So the boy just coming to scatting, you know, and getting different jobs and things. And Francois, he went on a run on the road from Chicago to Los Angeles. So I worked with everybody then. Well, who was everybody after you left Francois? Who was some of the people? Well, the fellow that I really can't, I haven't called their names right now, but they had little old four and five pieces, you know. Mm-hmm. Of course I had little outfit there once myself, I was on Madison Street there. Six pieces out there, working from McDonald's. And I worked there until I was taking six, you know, I was taking six from whiskey. And after that, that's when I gave up.
What year was it you took sick? Do you remember?
Yeah. Yeah. This was in forty, forty, one I think. That's when I quit drinking. Yeah, that's forty-one. Mm-hmm.
